Verify Razor stripper
I've hit the tool limit for this turn, so let me hand you what's verified so far rather than a half-finished tarball. The good news is that the hard part — proving the mechanical transformation is safe — is largely done.

What the measurements say
Your suspicion was right, and it's worse than "verbose":

Category	Bytes	Share of tree
C# comments	1,602,203	21%
Razor comments	~272,000	3.5%
The four big docs	1,655,921	21%
Shell comments	~116,000	1.5%
Everything else	~4,050,000	53%
40.7% of all C# source is comments. The tree is 7.7 MB; roughly 3.6 MB of it is prose about the code rather than code.

Within TECHNICAL_SPECIFICATION.md (733 KB), three sections are 69% of the file: Appendix A (222 KB), the Changelog (144 KB), and §16 Testing (136 KB). Appendix A is a four-column table whose "What happened" column holds full paragraphs — and it duplicates DOCUMENTATION_REVIEW.md, which is the same 118 findings written again at length. That's one fact written twice, which is the exact shape F-48 and F-50 are about.

The C# stripper is done and clean
258 files, 1,602,203 bytes removed (43%), and it passes every invariant I could think to assert:

lexer finishes in code state in every file (handles raw strings of any fence length, verbatim, interpolated, nested strings inside interpolation holes, char literals)
{}, (), [] all balance
the literal stream is byte-identical before and after — no string was damaged
idempotent
every original line containing no comment marker survives verbatim
[Fact]/[Theory] counts unchanged in all 114 test files
no CR, no whitespace-only lines, exactly one final newline
Landmines I found before touching anything
These are the reason this can't be a one-pass job:

DocumentationCommentContractTests.cs has MinimumBlocksScanned = 1_500. Strip the /// blocks and this gate fails instantly. Its subject stops existing, so under F-41 the honest move is to delete the gate, not lower the floor — plus its §16.4 paragraph and a ledger row.
GenerateDocumentationFile is false — so no CS1591 storm. Cleared.
TestingSectionContractTests requires ≥37 paragraphs in §16.4, each naming exactly one *Tests.cs and one matching assertion count. It reads raw file text, so a [Fact] inside a comment would shift a count — I checked all 114 files, none do. Counts are stable.
Eight scripts implement --help by printing their own header comment block (backup.sh, check_tree.sh, check_repository.sh, dev_instance.sh, ci_local.sh, restore.sh, restore_drill.sh, check_compose_substitution.sh). Those headers are functional. They get condensed by hand, not stripped.
MarkdownTableContractTests floors: ≥12 documents, ≥30 tables, ≥200 rows. You're at 51 tables / 480 rows. A careless doc rewrite that collapses BUILD_PROGRESS.md's 23 tables into one drops you to ~29 tables — red. The rewrite has to be deliberately table-shaped.
docs/progress/BUILD_PROGRESS_THROUGH_M6_SLICE_39.md must stay linked by exact path from a dumped document, and it's withheld so I can't see it. That string is preserved verbatim.
SpecificationVersionTests means the Changelog can be truncated freely as long as the newest entry matches the header and entries descend — that's ~130 KB for free.
check_repository.sh needs README→SECURITY, CONTRIBUTING→SECURITY, SECURITY→CONTRIBUTING edges plus §17 and "Report a vulnerability" in SECURITY.md.
The project already has SourceCode.WithoutComments (F-116), so gates that scan for code strip comments first and are immune — that's a big help.

Where I stopped
The Razor stripper reported 50 "lost line" hits. These are false positives in my verifier, not stripper bugs — every one is an interior line of a multi-line @* ... *@ block that doesn't itself contain @* or *@, so my "line had no comment marker, so it must survive" rule wrongly demanded it survive. The verifier needs to exclude lines inside comment spans. Nothing is actually broken, but I won't ship 51 Razor files on an assertion I haven't fixed.

Still to do
Fix the Razor verifier's span tracking, re-verify the 51 files
Shell stripper (heredoc-aware, shebang-preserving, hand-condensed --help headers), plus SQL / CSS / JS
Delete DocumentationCommentContractTests.cs; repair §16.4 to exactly 37+ paragraphs with correct counts
Author the condensed docs: spec (→ ~55 KB), ledger as a 118-row table (→ ~25 KB), build log as a slice index, menu plan, operations, README, requirements, _CHANGES.md
Re-run every gate by emulation, with sensitivity proofs
Package the tarball, with the delete list and git add callouts
One decision I need from you
The ADRs are 76 KB total — 1% of the tree. Condensing 15 files for 40 KB is real regression risk (ADR-0008 holds one of the 30 required tables) for almost no capacity gain. My recommendation is to leave them exactly as they are.

More substantively: I can either delete the verbose doc history outright, or move it into docs/progress/, which export.sh already withholds from the dump. The second keeps every word in the working tree and in git while shrinking dump.txt just as much — and it's the pattern you already established in Slice 46 under F-96. Deletion is cleaner; archiving is reversible. Say which and I'll build it that way.

Shall I continue from here?

The project already has SourceCode.WithoutComments (F-116), so gates that scan for code strip comments first and are immune — that's a big help.

Where I stopped
The Razor stripper reported 50 "lost line" hits. These are false positives in my verifier, not stripper bugs — every one is an interior line of a multi-line @* ... *@ block that doesn't itself contain @* or *@, so my "line had no comment marker, so it must survive" rule wrongly demanded it survive. The verifier needs to exclude lines inside comment spans. Nothing is actually broken, but I won't ship 51 Razor files on an assertion I haven't fixed.
